In `test_ean_def_use_case`, `fake.ean(length=8, prefixes=("12",))` calls `Provider.ean`, which immediately delegates to `_ean(length, prefixes=prefixes)`. Inside `_ean`, the `length` and `prefixes` parameters are read in the validation and branch conditions, `code` is defined by the list comprehension and then read when applying the prefix, when computing the weighted sum, when appending the check digit, and when building the return string. Because `prefixes` is non-empty, `prefix` is assigned and then read to slice and map into `code`; because `length == 8`, the `weights` assignment on the EAN-8 branch is the one later used. Finally, `weighted_sum` is read to compute `check_digit`, and `check_digit` is read when appended to `code`.
